value.statement: died suddenly without illness thirty li outside the provincial capital

value.statement: died upon reaching home after begging leave for illness

units.zh: 彭而述，字子籛，河南鄧州人。
units.en: Peng Ershu, courtesy name Ziliu, came from Dengzhou in Henan.
units.literal: Peng Ershu, styled Ziliu, was a native of Dengzhou in Henan.

units.zh: 明崇禎進士，官陽曲知縣，母憂歸。
units.en: He had passed the jinshi examination in the Chongzhen era of the Ming and served as magistrate of Yangqu; when his mother died, he left office to mourn.
units.literal: He was a jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, served as magistrate of Yangqu, and returned home upon his mother's death.

units.zh: 順治初，英親王徇湖廣，薦為提學僉事，遷永州道參議。
units.en: In the early Shunzhi period, when the Prince of Ying led troops through Huguang, Peng was recommended as educational intendant and soon promoted to assistant administrator of Yongzhou Circuit.
units.literal: Early in Shunzhi, when the Prince of Ying campaigned through Huguang, he was recommended as educational intendant and later transferred to assistant administrator of Yongzhou Circuit.

units.zh: 孔有德定湖南，薦而述授貴州巡撫，予兵三千以行。
units.en: After Kong Youde pacified Hunan, he had Ershu appointed governor of Guizhou and supplied him with three thousand soldiers for the expedition.
units.literal: When Kong Youde pacified Hunan, he recommended Ershu for appointment as governor of Guizhou and gave him three thousand troops for the journey.

units.zh: 次靖州，降將陳友龍叛，圍州城，而述夜開西門出，營山下，選勁騎乘霧衝陣，賊潰且走，副將賀進才戰死。
units.en: Near Jingzhou the surrendered general Chen Youlong rose in revolt and besieged the city. Ershu slipped out through the west gate by night, made camp below the hills, and sent picked cavalry charging through the mist; the rebels broke and fled, though Vice-General He Jincai was killed in the fighting.
units.literal: When he reached Jingzhou, the surrendered general Chen Youlong rebelled and besieged the prefectural city. Ershu opened the west gate at night and went out, encamped below the mountain, selected elite cavalry to charge through the fog, the rebels were routed and fled, and Vice-General He Jincai died in battle.

units.zh: 城兵大噪，欲與友龍合，而述拔眾退守寶慶，告有德益師，與賊相持紫陽河上。
units.en: The city garrison clamored to join Chen Youlong, but Ershu pulled his men back to hold Baoqing, asked Youde for reinforcements, and fought the enemy to a standstill on the Ziyang River.
units.literal: The garrison troops made a great uproar, wishing to join Chen Youlong, but Ershu withdrew his forces to hold Baqing, reported to Youde to send more troops, and stalemate with the rebels along the Ziyang River.

units.zh: 永州陷，劾免官。
units.en: After Yongzhou fell he was impeached and removed from office.
units.literal: When Yongzhou fell, he was impeached and dismissed from office.

units.zh: 吳三桂徵水西土司安坤，而述謀曰：「烏蒙、烏撒、鎮雄、東川四府與水西為脣齒，土司隴安籓又與安氏婚媾。
units.en: When Wu Sangui marched against An Kun, the Shuixi chieftain, Ershu counseled him: "Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan stand with Shuixi like lip and teeth, and the chieftain Long Anfan is tied to the An family by marriage as well.
units.literal: When Wu Sangui campaigned against An Kun, the native chieftain of Shuixi, Ershu advised: "The four prefectures of Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan are lip and teeth to Shuixi, and the native chieftain Long Anfan is also allied by marriage with the An clan.

units.zh: 今四府雖名內附，狼子野心，勢必顧惜其種類。
units.en: Although those four prefectures now profess allegiance, their hearts are wolfish; they are bound to protect their own people.
units.literal: Though the four prefectures are now nominally submitted, they have the heart of a wolf cub and will surely look after their own kind.

units.zh: 以水西之強，而安籓與四府附之，安坤未易制也。
units.en: Shuixi is strong, and with Anfan and the four prefectures behind it, An Kun will not be easily brought to heel.
units.literal: With Shuixi's strength, and Anfan and the four prefectures supporting it, An Kun will not be easy to subdue.

units.zh: 莫如先定四府，馘安籓，然後西南可無患。」
units.en: Better to secure the four prefectures first and eliminate Anfan; only then can the southwest be kept free of trouble."
units.literal: It would be best first to secure the four prefectures and kill Anfan; then the southwest can be free of trouble."

units.zh: 三桂用其策，誅安坤。
units.en: Sangui took his advice and put An Kun to death.
units.literal: Sangui adopted his plan and executed An Kun.

units.zh: 遷廣西右布政使。
units.en: He was promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangxi.
units.literal: He was transferred to be Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangxi.

units.zh: 三桂薦為雲南左布政使，而述乞歸，三桂留之，會有詔召，遂行，出會城三十里，一夕無疾卒。
units.en: Sangui recommended him for Left Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan. Ershu asked to retire, but Sangui kept him until an imperial summons came; he then departed, and thirty li outside the capital he died suddenly in the night without any known illness.
units.literal: Sangui recommended him as Left Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan. Ershu begged to return home; Sangui detained him, but when an imperial summons arrived he set out, and thirty li beyond the provincial capital he died suddenly in a single night without prior illness.

units.zh: 陸振芬，字令遠，江南華亭人。
units.en: Lu Zhenfen, courtesy name Lingyuan, came from Huating in Jiangnan.
units.literal: Lu Zhenfen, styled Lingyuan, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 順治六年進士。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi.
units.literal: He was a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi.

units.zh: 時兩粵未平，廷議破格用人，即新進士中遴才除道府。
units.en: The two Guang provinces were still unsettled, and the court decided to break with precedent by choosing talented new jinshi for circuit and prefectural appointments.
units.literal: At that time the two Guang provinces were not yet pacified; the court debated appointing men outside the usual rules and selecting talented new jinshi for circuit and prefectural posts.

units.zh: 振芬授廣東惠潮道副使，從師南征。
units.en: Zhenfen was made vice commissioner of Huichao Circuit in Guangdong and marched south with the expeditionary force.
units.literal: Zhenfen was appointed vice commissioner of the Huichao Circuit in Guangdong and followed the army south.

units.zh: 是冬，克南雄。
units.en: That winter Nanxiong was taken.
units.literal: That winter they captured Nanxiong.

units.zh: 七年春，度大庾嶺，次韶州。
units.en: In the spring of the seventh year they crossed the Dayu Mountains and encamped at Shaozhou.
units.literal: In the spring of the seventh year they crossed the Dayu Range and halted at Shaozhou.

units.zh: 韶州以南望風降，進規會城，既下，振芬與總兵郭虎率師赴惠州，剿撫歸善、海豐諸寨。
units.en: Everything south of Shaozhou surrendered at the first approach; after the provincial capital fell, Zhenfen and Commander Guo Hu took forces to Huizhou to subdue and win over the stockades of Guishan, Haifeng, and the rest.
units.literal: South of Shaozhou all submitted at the news; they advanced on the provincial capital, and after it fell Zhenfen and Commander Guo Hu led troops to Huizhou to suppress and pacify the stockades of Guishan, Haifeng, and others.

units.zh: 將至，諸寨窺兵寡，出拒。
units.en: As they drew near, the stockades, seeing how few troops they had, sallied out to fight.
units.literal: As they were about to arrive, the stockades saw that the troops were few and came out to resist.

units.zh: 振芬選精銳數百人繞出其旁擊之，獲一隊，諸寨皆懼。
units.en: Zhenfen picked several hundred crack troops to swing around and hit them from the flank, took one whole company prisoner, and every stockade was shaken.
units.literal: Zhenfen selected several hundred elite troops to circle around and strike them from the flank, capturing one company, and all the stockades were afraid.

units.zh: 於是諭以禍福，降者踵至。
units.en: He then explained the consequences they faced, and surrendering parties came in one after another.
units.literal: Thereupon he lectured them on gain and loss, and those who surrendered came one after another.

units.zh: 至海豐，守者抗不下。
units.en: At Haifeng the defenders held out and the place would not fall.
units.literal: At Haifeng the defenders resisted and the city could not be taken.

units.zh: 振芬與虎駐五坡驛，他將自羊氾嶺會師合攻之，遂克其城。
units.en: Zhenfen and Hu camped at Wupo Post while other commanders converged from Yangfan Ridge for a joint attack, and the city was finally taken.
units.literal: Zhenfen and Hu encamped at Wupo Post; other generals joined from Yangfan Ridge for a combined assault, and they then took the city.

units.zh: 碣石衛亦降。
units.en: Jieshi Guard surrendered as well.
units.literal: Jieshi Guard also surrendered.

units.zh: 八年，抵潮州，上官，聯結諸鎮，檢制土官，招集流亡，簡省徭役，民始有更生之樂。
units.en: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou and took up his post, coordinated the garrisons, kept native officials in check, brought back refugees, and cut back corvée burdens, until the people finally felt life returning.
units.literal: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou and assumed office, linked the garrisons, restrained native officials, gathered the displaced, and reduced corvée levies, so the people at last knew the joy of rebirth.

units.zh: 亂甫定，用法嚴，郡縣輒濫禁無辜。
units.en: With the rebellion only just ended, the law was enforced harshly and prefectures and counties often jailed innocent people at will.
units.literal: The turmoil had just subsided and the law was applied strictly; prefectures and counties often imprisoned the innocent without cause.

units.zh: 振芬與屬吏約，期五十日清庶獄，囹圄為空。
units.en: Zhenfen pledged to his staff that they would clear the backlog of ordinary cases within fifty days, and the prisons were emptied.
units.literal: Zhenfen agreed with his subordinates to clear the common prisons within fifty days, and the jails were emptied.

units.zh: 九年，會師復平遠，總兵郝尚久故降將，陰持兩端，聞將改授水師副總兵，結山海諸寇僭立帥府。
units.en: In the ninth year allied forces retook Pingyuan. Commander Hao Shangjiu, once a Ming defector, had long hedged his loyalty; when he learned he was to be transferred to a naval vice command, he joined coastal and mountain rebels in setting up a rival headquarters.
units.literal: In the ninth year the armies reunited to recover Pingyuan. Commander Hao Shangjiu, a former surrendered general, secretly wavered between two sides; hearing he was to be reassigned as vice commander of the naval forces, he joined the mountain and sea bandits in arrogating a commander's headquarters.

units.zh: 振芬牒大吏策弭變，不應。
units.en: Zhenfen sent the senior officials a memorial outlining how to head off the revolt, but they did not act on it.
units.literal: Zhenfen memorialized the high officials with a plan to quell the disturbance, but received no response.

units.zh: 十年春，尚久自署新泰侯，舉兵圍道署。
units.en: In the spring of the tenth year Shangjiu declared himself Marquis of Xintai and marched on the circuit yamen.
units.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Shangjiu styled himself Marquis of Xintai and raised troops to besiege the circuit yamen.

units.zh: 振芬諭以大義，不從，使告變。
units.en: Zhenfen appealed to him on grounds of loyalty, but Shangjiu refused to listen, and Zhenfen sent word of the uprising.
units.literal: Zhenfen admonished him with the greater duty, but he would not listen, so Zhenfen sent word of the rebellion.

units.zh: 秋，固山兵至，振芬約為內應，引外兵入，誅尚久。
units.en: That autumn the banner garrison troops arrived; Zhenfen had arranged an inside response, admitted the relief force, and Shangjiu was put to death.
units.literal: In autumn the garrison troops arrived; Zhenfen had arranged to act from within, led the outside troops in, and executed Shangjiu.

units.zh: 事平，引疾歸里。
units.en: After order was restored he cited illness and retired to his home district.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, he pleaded illness and returned home.

units.zh: 家居四十年乃卒。
units.en: He lived in retirement for forty years before he died.
units.literal: He lived at home for forty years before he died.

units.zh: 姚延著，字象懸，浙江烏程人。
units.en: Yao Yanzhu, courtesy name Xiangxuan, came from Wucheng in Zhejiang.
units.literal: Yao Yanzhu, styled Xiangxuan, was a native of Wucheng in Zhejiang.

units.zh: 順治六年進士，除廣西慶遠知府。
units.en: After passing the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.
units.literal: A jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.

units.zh: 從師南征，調柳州，有守禦功，又調平樂。
units.en: He marched south with the army, was posted to Liuzhou where he distinguished himself in defense, and was later moved to Pingle.
units.literal: He followed the army south, was transferred to Liuzhou where he had merit in defense, and was then transferred to Pingle.

units.zh: 遷廣東嶺南道副使，撫僮寨，擢江南按察使。
units.en: He rose to vice commissioner of Lingnan Circuit in Guangdong, pacified Zhuang stockades, and was then promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan.
units.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of Lingnan Circuit in Guangdong, pacified Zhuang stockades, and was elevated to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan.

units.zh: 十六年，鄭成功內犯，陷鎮江，入攻江寧。
units.en: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong raided inland, captured Zhenjiang, and pressed the attack on Jiangning.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong invaded inland, took Zhenjiang, and advanced to attack Jiangning.

units.zh: 延著佐總督郎廷佐繕守備，安輯危城，閭閻不擾。
units.en: Yanzhu assisted Governor Lang Tingzuo in organizing the defenses, steadied the besieged city, and kept the populace from panic.
units.literal: Yanzhu assisted Governor Lang Tingzuo in preparing defenses, settled the endangered city, and the neighborhoods were not disturbed.

units.zh: 民間時有羊尾黨，事發，株連數百人。
units.en: A faction known as the Yangwei Party had appeared among the people; when the case broke, several hundred were dragged in.
units.literal: Among the people there was at times the Yangwei Party; when the affair broke, several hundred were implicated.

units.zh: 延著謂廷佐曰：「寇在門，不可興大獄、搖人心。」
units.en: Yanzhu told Tingzuo: "The enemy is at our gates—we cannot open a sweeping trial and unsettle the people."
units.literal: Yanzhu said to Tingzuo: "The enemy is at the gate; we must not launch a great prosecution and shake the people's hearts."

units.zh: 獄乃解。
units.en: The prosecution was dropped.
units.literal: The case was then closed.

units.zh: 當事急，人多疑貳，民間有宿怨，輒誣以通敵。
units.en: In the emergency many were suspected of disloyalty, and private feuds led to false charges of aiding the enemy.
units.literal: At the crisis many were suspected of wavering; where old grudges existed among the people, they were often falsely accused of colluding with the enemy.

units.zh: 延著嚴治反坐，多所全活。
units.en: Yanzhu cracked down hard on malicious prosecution and spared many innocent lives.
units.literal: Yanzhu strictly punished false accusation and thereby saved many lives.

units.zh: 城民有升高而望者，邏者執之，總管喀喀木以為敵諜，延著力爭，得不死。
units.en: Patrols seized a townsman who had climbed up to look around; Commander Kekemu judged him a spy, but Yanzhu argued fiercely and the man was spared execution.
units.literal: A townsman who climbed high to look about was seized by patrols; Commander Kekemu took him for an enemy spy, but Yanzhu argued strenuously and he was not put to death.

units.zh: 喀喀木部兵擾城市，延著捕得械斃之。
units.en: Troops under Kekemu were harassing the city; Yanzhu arrested the offenders and had them strangled.
units.literal: Kekemu's troops harassed the city; Yanzhu captured them and had them executed by strangulation.

units.zh: 吏卒私掠被難婦女，延著親駐江乾，召其家，遣還者一千七百人，以此忤喀喀木。
units.en: Clerks and soldiers were seizing women caught up in the turmoil; Yanzhu went in person to the riverbank, called their families forward, and restored seventeen hundred women to their homes—an act that put him at odds with Kekemu.
units.literal: Officials and soldiers privately seized women afflicted by the disaster; Yanzhu personally stationed himself on the riverbank, summoned their families, and sent back seventeen hundred persons, thereby offending Kekemu.

units.zh: 事定敘功，擢河南左布政使。
units.en: After peace was restored his service was recognized and he was promoted to Left Administrative Commissioner of Henan.
units.literal: When the affair was settled merits were recorded and he was promoted to Left Administrative Commissioner of Henan.

units.zh: 旋以憂歸，而金壇獄起。
units.en: He soon left office to mourn a parent, and then the Jintan case erupted.
units.literal: Soon afterward he returned home in mourning, and the Jintan case arose.

units.zh: 鎮江之陷也，屬縣戒嚴。
units.en: When Zhenjiang fell, the surrounding counties were put on alert.
units.literal: When Zhenjiang fell, the subordinate counties were placed under martial law.

units.zh: 金壇知縣任體坤集縣中士大夫王重、袁大受等謀遣諸生十輩詣鎮江乞緩兵。
units.en: Jintan's magistrate Ren Tikun gathered local scholars Wang Chong, Yuan Dashou, and others to send ten parties of students to Zhenjiang to beg for a ceasefire.
units.literal: The magistrate of Jintan, Ren Tikun, gathered the local gentry Wang Chong, Yuan Dashou, and others to plan sending ten groups of students to Zhenjiang to plead for a truce.

units.zh: 丹徒亂民王再興兵起，復令書吏、耆民數十人送款，盡竊庫帑以遁。
units.en: When the Dantu rebel Wang Zaixing rose in arms, Tikun again sent dozens of clerks and elders to offer submission—and they looted the treasury and fled.
units.literal: The rebel Wang Zai of Dantu raised troops; Tikun again sent dozens of clerks and elders to submit, and they stole all the treasury funds and fled.

units.zh: 喀喀木等擊敗成功，體坤乃復至縣，賂重、大受謁大吏，謂士民送款，冀掩棄城罪。
units.en: After Kekemu and the others routed Chenggong, Tikun returned to his post and bribed Chong and Dashou to lobby the senior officials, claiming the local elite had submitted in order to hide his own crime of deserting the county.
units.literal: Kekemu and others defeated Chenggong; Tikun then returned to the county, bribed Chong and Dashou to visit the high officials, and claimed the gentry and people had submitted, hoping to cover his crime of abandoning the city.

units.zh: 重、大受居鄉多不法，為諸生所撓。
units.en: Chong and Dashou had long bullied their home districts, and the students had stood in their way.
units.literal: Chong and Dashou had long committed many unlawful acts in their home districts and were thwarted by the students.

units.zh: 至是欲以叛坐諸生，泄私怨，列姓名以上。
units.en: They now sought to have the students convicted of treason to settle old scores and submitted a list of names.
units.literal: Now they wished to charge the students with rebellion to vent private grudges and submitted a list of names.

units.zh: 巡按馬勝聲疏聞，下廷佐令延著鞫其獄。
units.en: Censor Ma Shengsheng reported the matter to the throne; the case was referred to Tingzuo with orders for Yanzhu to hear it.
units.literal: Censor Ma Shengsheng memorialized the throne; the case was sent down to Tingzuo with orders for Yanzhu to try it.

units.zh: 延著縶縣吏李鍾秀，訊得實，欲但坐體坤，餘皆減罪。
units.en: Yanzhu arrested county clerk Li Zhongxiu, questioned him until the facts came out, and sought to punish only Tikun while leniency for the others.
units.literal: Yanzhu arrested the county clerk Li Zhongxiu, examined him and learned the truth, and wished to punish only Tikun while reducing the charges for the rest.

units.zh: 大受騰書京師為蜚語，欲並陷延著，御史馮班發其狀。
units.en: Dashou sent inflammatory letters to the capital hoping to drag Yanzhu down too, but Censor Feng Ban exposed what he was doing.
units.literal: Dashou sent letters to the capital spreading rumors, intending to implicate Yanzhu as well, but Censor Feng Ban exposed his conduct.

units.zh: 時侍郎尼滿奉詔勘提督馬逢知獄，命即訊，乃坐重、大受及諸士大夫集議者。
units.en: Vice Minister Niman had been sent by imperial order to investigate Governor-General Ma Fengzhi's case and was told to try this one immediately; he convicted Chong, Dashou, and the scholars who had joined the deliberations.
units.literal: At that time Vice Minister Niman was ordered by imperial edict to investigate the case of Governor-General Ma Fengzhi and was commanded to try this case at once; he convicted Chong, Dashou, and the gentry who had met in council.

units.zh: 諸生及書吏、耆民送款者皆斬，體坤以被逼迫減為絞。
units.en: The students and every clerk and elder who had offered submission were beheaded; Tikun, as one who had acted under duress, was sentenced to strangulation instead.
units.literal: The students and the clerks and elders who had submitted were all beheaded; Tikun, on the ground of coercion, had his sentence reduced to strangulation.

units.zh: 巡按何可化又疏劾延著讞從叛罪人史記青、管得勝傅輕比，又有王天福、韓王錫並縱不擬罪，與金壇獄並論，亦坐絞。
units.en: Censor He Kehua memorialized again, accusing Yanzhu of applying light statutes to the rebel criminals Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng, and of releasing Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi without punishment; lumped together with the Jintan affair, Yanzhu was also sentenced to strangulation.
units.literal: Censor He Kehua again memorialized impeaching Yanzhu for applying light comparisons to the rebel criminals Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng, and for releasing without sentence Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi; together with the Jintan case he too was sentenced to strangulation.

units.zh: 時喀喀木主軍事，新破敵，尤威重，素不慊於延著。
units.en: Kekemu then held military authority, had just crushed the enemy, and wielded exceptional power; he had long borne a grudge against Yanzhu.
units.literal: At that time Kekemu controlled military affairs, had newly defeated the enemy, and was especially formidable; he had long been displeased with Yanzhu.

units.zh: 民間謂延著之死，喀喀木實主之。
units.en: Popular rumor held that Kekemu was really the one who brought about Yanzhu's death.
units.literal: Among the people it was said that Kekemu was in fact behind Yanzhu's death.

units.zh: 就刑日，江寧為罷市，士民哭踴。
units.en: On the day he was executed Jiangning shut its markets; scholars and townspeople wept and stamped their feet in mourning.
units.literal: On the day of execution Jiangning closed its markets; scholars and commoners wept and stamped in grief.

units.zh: 喪歸，數百里祭奠不絕，建祠雞鳴山下私祀焉。
units.en: As his coffin was borne home, mourners offered sacrifices all along the route for hundreds of li, and a shrine was built below Jiming Hill where people worshipped him privately.
units.literal: When the coffin returned home, offerings continued without break for several hundred li, and a shrine was built below Jiming Hill for private worship.

units.zh: 子淳燾，康熙六年進士，授內閣中書舍人。
units.en: His son Chunxi passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
units.literal: His son Chunxi was a jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

units.zh: 伏闕上書為延著訟冤。
units.en: He knelt at the palace gate and submitted a memorial pleading his father's innocence.
units.literal: He prostrated himself before the palace gate and submitted a memorial to plead his father's innocence.

units.zh: 累擢湖廣提學道僉事，坐事罷，未行，值叛卒夏逢龍之亂，誓死不為屈。
units.en: He rose to educational intendant of Huguang Circuit, was dismissed for an offense before he could take up the post, and when the mutineer Xia Fenglong rebelled he swore he would die rather than yield.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to educational intendant of Huguang Circuit, was dismissed for an offense before he could take up the post, and when the mutineer Xia Fenglong rebelled he vowed to die rather than submit.

units.zh: 事聞，复官，授岳常澧道副使。
units.en: When his conduct was reported to the throne he was reinstated and appointed vice commissioner of Yuechangli Circuit.
units.literal: When the matter was reported he was restored to office and appointed vice commissioner of the Yuechangli Circuit.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 畢振姬，字亮四，山西高平人。
units.en: Bi Zhenji, courtesy name Liangsi, came from Gaoping in Shanxi.
units.literal: Bi Zhenji, styled Liangsi, was a native of Gaoping in Shanxi.

units.zh: 順治三年進士，授平陽教授。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed professor at Pingyang.
units.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed professor at Pingyang.

units.zh: 入為國子監助教，累遷刑部員外郎。
units.en: He entered the Imperial Academy as assistant instructor and rose through the ranks to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.
units.literal: He entered service as an assistant instructor in the Imperial Academy and was promoted in stages to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 曹事暇，獨坐陋室，布被瓦盆，讀書不稍倦。
units.en: In his spare time from office he would sit alone in a plain room with cotton bedding and earthenware bowls, reading without ever tiring.
units.literal: When official duties left him free, he sat alone in a humble room with cotton bedding and earthen bowls, reading without the slightest weariness.

units.zh: 十年，出為山東濟南道參議。
units.en: In the tenth year he was posted as assistant administrator of Jinan Circuit in Shandong.
units.literal: In the tenth year he went out to serve as assistant administrator of Jinan Circuit in Shandong.

units.zh: 歲旱，流民踞山谷為盜，振姬晝夜馳三百里往諭之，悉就撫，全活者七​​千餘人。
units.en: During a drought year refugees had turned bandits in the mountain valleys; Zhenji rode three hundred li day and night to reason with them, and all came in to be pacified—more than seven thousand lives spared.
units.literal: In a year of drought, displaced people occupied the mountain valleys as bandits; Zhenji rode day and night three hundred li to admonish them, and all submitted to pacification, saving more than seven thousand lives.

units.zh: 泰山香稅，歲羨餘七千金，例充公使錢，振姬悉以佐餉。
units.en: The Mount Tai incense tax produced an annual surplus of seven thousand taels, normally reserved for official travel expenses; Zhenji applied all of it to army rations.
units.literal: The incense tax of Mount Tai yielded a surplus of seven thousand taels yearly, which by rule went to official travel funds; Zhenji devoted it all to military provisions.

units.zh: 調廣東驛傳道僉事。
units.en: He was transferred to intendant of the Post Relay Circuit in Guangdong.
units.literal: He was transferred to be intendant of the Post Relay Circuit in Guangdong.

units.zh: 時三籓使命往來絡繹，胥吏乘以私派折價，民苦之，振姬一繩以法，閱數月，減船數百，減​​費七萬有奇。
units.en: With the Three Feudatories' envoys constantly passing through, clerks imposed illegal surcharges and skimmed payments, to the people's misery. Zhenji enforced the law without favor; within months he cut several hundred boats from service and saved more than seventy thousand taels.
units.literal: At that time the missions of the Three Feudatories came and went incessantly; clerks took the opportunity for private levies and discount extortion, and the people suffered. Zhenji applied the law uniformly; within several months he reduced boats by several hundred and cut costs by more than seventy thousand.

units.zh: 調浙江金衢嚴道參政，擢廣西按察使。
units.en: He was moved to administrator of Jinquyan Circuit in Zhejiang and then promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
units.literal: He was transferred to be administrator of the Jinquyan Circuit in Zhejiang and promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.

units.zh: 所至以廉能聞。
units.en: Everywhere he served he won a reputation for integrity and ability.
units.literal: Wherever he went he was known for integrity and competence.

units.zh: 遷湖廣布政使，乞病歸。
units.en: He was promoted to administrative commissioner of Huguang, then asked to retire on grounds of illness.
units.literal: He was transferred to administrative commissioner of Huguang and begged leave on grounds of illness to return home.

units.zh: 康熙中，詔舉博學鴻儒，左都御史魏裔介、副都御史劉楗疏薦之。
units.en: During the Kangxi reign an edict summoned recommendations of learned scholars; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jian both memorialized in his favor.
units.literal: In the Kangxi reign an edict called for recommending erudite scholars; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jian memorialized recommending him.

units.zh: 十八年，命廷臣舉清廉吏，裔介复疏言：「振姬清操絕世，才略過人。
units.en: In the eighteenth year the court ordered officials to nominate incorrupt administrators; Yijie memorialized again: "Zhenji's integrity is unrivaled in our time, and his talent and strategic ability surpass ordinary men.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year the court ordered officials to recommend incorrupt administrators; Yijie again memorialized: "Zhenji's integrity is unmatched in the age, and his talent and strategy surpass others.

units.zh: 請告十餘年，躬耕百畝，讀書不輟。」
units.en: He has been retired for more than ten years, farming a hundred mu with his own hands, and has never stopped his studies."
units.literal: He has been on leave for more than ten years, personally tilling a hundred mu, and has never ceased reading."

units.zh: 楗亦言：「振姬居官不染一塵。
units.en: Jian also wrote: "In office Zhenji never soiled his hands with the slightest gain.
units.literal: Jian also said: "In office Zhenji did not take a speck of dust.

units.zh: 歸日一僕一馬，了無長物，真學行兼優之人。」
units.en: When he went home he had only one servant and one horse and owned nothing else—a man who truly united learning and character."
units.literal: When he returned home he had but one servant and one horse and possessed nothing more—truly a man of combined learning and conduct."

units.zh: 下部議，以振姬老，置勿用。
units.en: The ministries deliberated and, on the ground of Zhenji's age, set the recommendation aside without appointing him.
units.literal: The matter was sent to the ministries for deliberation; because Zhenji was old, he was set aside and not employed.

units.zh: 尋卒。
units.en: He died not long after.
units.literal: Soon afterward he died.

units.zh: 方國棟，字幹霄，順天宛平人。
units.en: Fang Guodong, courtesy name Ganxiao, came from Wanping in Shuntian.
units.literal: Fang Guodong, styled Ganxiao, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian.

units.zh: 順治三年舉人，授蠡縣教諭。
units.en: He passed the provincial examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed county instructor of Li.
units.literal: A provincial graduate in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed instructor of Li County.

units.zh: 入為國子監助教，累擢至刑部郎中。
units.en: He entered the Imperial Academy as assistant instructor and rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
units.literal: He entered as an assistant instructor in the Imperial Academy and was promoted in stages to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 十六年，出為廣東海北道僉事。
units.en: In the sixteenth year he was posted as intendant of Haibei Circuit in Guangdong.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year he went out to serve as intendant of the Haibei Circuit in Guangdong.

units.zh: 海寇鄧耀居島中，時出剽掠。
units.en: The pirate Deng Yao lived on an offshore island and raided the coast from time to time.
units.literal: The sea bandit Deng Yao lived on an island and often came out to plunder.

units.zh: 國棟以三千人分五道進剿，檄鄰道出兵扼要隘，擒耀，解散餘黨。
units.en: Guodong took three thousand men in five columns against them, called on neighboring circuits to block the key passes, captured Yao, and broke up the remaining band.
units.literal: Guodong led three thousand men in five columns to suppress them, ordered neighboring circuits to send troops to hold the strategic passes, captured Yao, and dispersed the remaining followers.

units.zh: 事平，雷、廉兩部諸富人為賊所誣，械系者眾，國棟察其冤，為辨雪。
units.en: After order was restored, many wealthy men in Lei and Lian prefectures had been framed by the pirates and thrown in chains; Guodong found them innocent and secured their release.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, many wealthy men of Lei and Lian prefectures had been falsely accused by the bandits and were shackled in large numbers; Guodong saw their innocence and cleared them.

units.zh: 諸富人裒千金為報，國棟曰：「吾憫若無辜，柰何污我？」
units.en: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels to thank him; Guodong said, "I pitied your innocence—why would you try to bribe me?"
units.literal: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels as a reward; Guodong said: "I pitied your innocence—why would you try to stain me?"

units.zh: 卻之。
units.en: He refused the gift.
units.literal: He refused it.

units.zh: 遷山西寧武道參議。
units.en: He was transferred to assistant administrator of Ningwu Circuit in Shanxi.
units.literal: He was transferred to be assistant administrator of Ningwu Circuit in Shanxi.

units.zh: 康熙六年裁缺，改江南蘇松常道參議。
units.en: When his post was abolished in the sixth year of Kangxi, he was reassigned as assistant administrator of Susongchang Circuit in Jiangnan.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi his post was abolished; he was reassigned as assistant administrator of the Susongchang Circuit in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 太湖堤岸傾圮，率吏民修葺，修沿海墩台及吳淞、劉河兩徬，工費不擾民。
units.en: When the Lake Tai dikes gave way, he led officials and commoners in repairs, rebuilt coastal watch towers and the Wusong and Liuhe embankments, and kept the labor levies from burdening the people.
units.literal: The dikes on Lake Tai collapsed; he led officials and people to repair them, restored coastal watch towers and the two embankments of Wusong and Liuhe, and the work costs did not trouble the people.

units.zh: 師下閩、粵，徵調旁午，國棟一意與民休息，每遇急徵，從容部署。
units.en: As imperial forces marched into Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions poured in without pause; Guodong was determined to give the people respite, and whenever urgent demands arrived he met them with calm planning.
units.literal: When the army descended on Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions came in rapid succession; Guodong was wholly intent on letting the people rest, and whenever urgent levies arrived he deployed resources calmly.

units.zh: 芻茭糧糗，預儲以待，軍興無乏，閭左晏然。
units.en: He stockpiled fodder and grain ahead of time so that when troops mobilized nothing ran short, and the common people lived in peace.
units.literal: Fodder and grain rations were stored in advance to await need; when the army mobilized nothing was lacking, and the neighborhoods were tranquil.

units.zh: 戒屬吏無朘民，郡縣稍稍知斂戢，不敢事剝削。
units.en: He warned his staff against squeezing the people, and prefectures and counties gradually learned to restrain themselves and ceased their extortions.
units.literal: He admonished subordinates not to squeeze the people; prefectures and counties gradually learned restraint and dared not practice extortion.

units.zh: 連歲用兵，度支不給，詔各省籌裕餉之策。
units.en: Years of warfare had drained the treasury, and an edict ordered every province to propose ways to secure adequate military funds.
units.literal: War continued year after year and the treasury could not meet expenses; an edict ordered each province to devise plans for adequate military funds.

units.zh: 國棟言：「古今生財之說，開與節二者而已。
units.en: Guodong wrote: "Throughout history, raising revenue has come down to only two things: finding new sources and cutting expenses.
units.literal: Guodong said: "Throughout history theories of generating wealth come down to only two things: opening sources and economizing.

units.zh: 議開於今日，已無可加，當議節，自朝廷始。
units.en: As for opening new sources today, there is little left to do; we should economize, and that must begin at court.
units.literal: To discuss opening sources today, there is nothing more to add; we should discuss economizing, beginning with the court itself.

units.zh: 舊制，江南歲市布五萬匹供宮府賚予，宜可罷，歲省帑金三萬。」
units.en: Under the old rules Jiangnan supplies fifty thousand bolts of cloth yearly for palace gifts; that practice should end, saving thirty thousand taels a year."
units.literal: By old regulation Jiangnan yearly markets fifty thousand bolts of cloth for palace grants; this should be abolished, saving thirty thousand taels from the treasury each year."

units.zh: 議上，報可，滿洲兵駐防蘇州，議築營舍於王府基，當城中。
units.en: The memorial was approved. When Manchu troops were garrisoned at Suzhou, officials proposed building barracks on the old princely mansion site in the heart of the city.
units.literal: The proposal was submitted and approved. Manchu troops garrisoned Suzhou; it was proposed to build barracks on the old princely mansion site in the center of the city.

units.zh: 國棟以兵民雜居難久安，持不可，乃改營南城隙地，民便之。
units.en: Guodong argued that soldiers and civilians could not live mixed together in stability and firmly opposed the plan; the barracks were moved to open ground in the southern city instead, to the people's relief.
units.literal: Guodong held that soldiers and civilians living mixed could not long remain stable and firmly opposed it; barracks were then placed on vacant land in the southern city, to the people's convenience.

units.zh: 宜興善權山中寺僧與豪族爭地，聚眾焚寺殺僧，知縣告亂，大吏將發兵。
units.en: In the Shanquan mountains of Yixing, temple monks were locked in a land dispute with powerful families; a mob burned the temple and killed monks. The magistrate reported an uprising and senior officials prepared to send troops.
units.literal: At Shanchansi in Shanquan, Yixing, monks disputed land with powerful clans; they gathered a mob, burned the temple, and killed monks. The magistrate reported rebellion and high officials were about to send troops.

units.zh: 國棟單騎馳往，得首禍寘法，餘無所問。
units.en: Guodong rode out alone, arrested the ringleaders and punished them under the law, and pressed no further inquiries.
units.literal: Guodong rode alone in haste to the scene, seized the ringleaders and punished them by law, and questioned no one else.

units.zh: 吳俗健訟，喜投缿告密，國棟輒不問，即有所案，亦從寬。
units.en: The people of Wu were litigious and fond of anonymous denunciations; Guodong generally ignored them, and even when he took up a case he dealt leniently.
units.literal: Wu custom was fond of litigation and delighted in dropping accusations into the complaint box; Guodong routinely paid no heed, and even when there were cases he was lenient.

units.zh: 馭吏嚴，而拊循士民具有恩意。
units.en: He was strict with his staff yet treated scholars and townspeople with genuine kindness.
units.literal: He was strict with subordinates, yet in comforting scholars and commoners he showed real kindness.

units.zh: 十六年，卒。
units.en: In the sixteenth year he died.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.

units.zh: 吳民思之，建祠虎丘山麓以祀。
units.en: The people of Wu missed him and built a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill in his memory.
units.literal: The people of Wu missed him and built a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill to worship him.

units.zh: 於朋舉，字襄子，江南金壇人。
units.en: Yu Pengju, courtesy name Xiangzi, came from Jintan in Jiangnan.
units.literal: Yu Pengju, styled Xiangzi, was a native of Jintan in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 順治六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and upon completing his training was appointed reviser.
units.literal: A jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.

units.zh: 十二年，出為河南睢陳道副使，政不擾民。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was posted as vice commissioner of Suichen Circuit in Henan, governing without harassing the people.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as vice commissioner of the Suichen Circuit in Henan; his administration did not trouble the people.

units.zh: 郾城盜殺縣官而逸，士民洶洶，謂城將受屠。
units.en: Bandits at Yancheng killed the county magistrate and escaped; the townspeople panicked, fearing the city would be put to the sword.
units.literal: At Yancheng bandits killed the county magistrate and fled; gentry and people were in uproar, saying the city would be massacred.

units.zh: 朋舉馳至，撫諭毋恐。
units.en: Pengju rode there at once, reassured the people, and told them not to be afraid.
units.literal: Pengju hurried there and comforted them, telling them not to fear.

units.zh: 營將以兵至，拒不使入城。
units.en: When a garrison commander marched up with troops, Pengju refused to let them enter the city.
units.literal: A garrison commander was bringing troops; Pengju refused to let them enter the city.

units.zh: 大吏召朋舉詰責，對曰：「郾城令，朋舉婦翁也。
units.en: A senior official summoned Pengju to rebuke him; he answered: "The magistrate of Yancheng is my wife's father.
units.literal: A high official summoned Pengju to rebuke him; he replied: "The magistrate of Yancheng is Pengju's father-in-law.

units.zh: 豈不欲甘心是盜？
units.en: Do you think I would not want those bandits punished?
units.literal: Would I not wish to take satisfaction on those bandits?

units.zh: 獨柰何苦良民！」
units.en: But why should innocent people suffer for it!"
units.literal: Only why must innocent people suffer!"

units.zh: 大吏悟，止兵，亦得盜正其罪。
units.en: The senior official understood, held back the troops, and the bandits were still brought to justice.
units.literal: The high official understood, halted the troops, and the bandits were also brought to justice.

units.zh: 遷福建福寧道參政。
units.en: He was transferred to administrator of Funing Circuit in Fujian.
units.literal: He was transferred to be administrator of Funing Circuit in Fujian.

units.zh: 興化瀕海，鎮將所部皆群盜受撫者。
units.en: Xinghua lay on the coast; the regional commander's troops were all former bandits who had accepted pacification.
units.literal: Xinghua bordered the sea; the troops under the regional commander were all bandit gangs who had submitted to pacification.

units.zh: 有材官辱張氏僕，張氏以告。
units.en: An officer humiliated a servant of the Zhang family, and the Zhangs lodged a complaint.
units.literal: An officer insulted a servant of the Zhang family, and the Zhangs reported it.

units.zh: 鎮將撻材官，部卒大譁，毀張氏之室，欲劫鎮將為亂。
units.en: The commander had the officer flogged; his men mutinied, wrecked the Zhang house, and tried to seize their commander and rise in revolt.
units.literal: The commander flogged the officer; the troops made a great uproar, wrecked the Zhang residence, and wished to seize the commander and rebel.

units.zh: 鎮將避去，則縊被撻者寘張氏，謂其僕殺之。
units.en: The commander fled; the mutineers hanged the flogged man and left the body at the Zhangs' door, claiming their servant had murdered him.
units.literal: The commander fled; they then hanged the man who had been flogged and placed the body at the Zhangs', claiming their servant had killed him.

units.zh: 朋舉甫到官，廉得首惡，猝縛至，集文武吏會鞫，健兒帶刀環立瞋視。
units.en: Pengju had just taken office; he traced the ringleaders, had them seized at once, and convened civil and military officials for a joint hearing while armed braves ringed the hall glaring.
units.literal: Pengju had just taken office; he investigated and found the ringleaders, suddenly bound them and brought them in, gathered civil and military officials for joint trial, while braves with swords stood glaring in a ring.

units.zh: 朋舉從容曰：「若曹幹軍法，罪重。
units.en: Pengju said calmly: "You have violated military law—a grave offense.
units.literal: Pengju said calmly: "You have violated military law; the crime is grave.

units.zh: 念若曹約束無素，但用殺人律，罪有專屬。」
units.en: Since you have never been properly disciplined, we will apply only the statute on homicide—the guilty party must be identified."
units.literal: Considering that you have never been disciplined, we will apply only the statute on homicide; the crime has its proper bearer."

units.zh: 眾乃泥首，言殺人者為張氏僕。
units.en: The men then kowtowed and claimed the killer was the Zhangs' servant.
units.literal: The crowd then pressed their foreheads to the ground and said the killer was the Zhangs' servant.

units.zh: 朋舉曰：「若曹氣焰何等，彼能於千百健兒中奪一人縊之耶？」
units.en: Pengju said: "With your swagger, could a mere servant seize one of you among a thousand armed men and hang him?"
units.literal: Pengju said: "What sort of spirit do you have—could he seize one man among a thousand braves and hang him?"

units.zh: 召訊證者，俱吐實，誅三人而事定。
units.en: He called witnesses; all confessed, three were executed, and the matter was closed.
units.literal: He summoned witnesses for questioning; all told the truth, three were executed, and the affair was settled.

units.zh: 泉州提督剿海盜，盜逸入興化界，鎮將獲數百人。
units.en: The provincial admiral of Quanzhou pursued sea pirates; the pirates fled into Xinghua and the regional commander seized several hundred.
units.literal: The Quanzhou provincial admiral suppressed sea pirates; the pirates fled into Xinghua territory and the regional commander captured several hundred.

units.zh: 朋舉視其嘗薙發者，曰：「此良民被陷，當宥。」
units.en: Seeing those who had already shaved their heads, Pengju said: "These are innocent people caught up in the affair—they should be spared."
units.literal: Pengju looked at those who had once tonsured their hair and said: "These are innocent people who were trapped; they should be pardoned."

units.zh: 有年少者，曰：「童穉何知，又當宥。」
units.en: Among them were youths; he said: "Children know nothing of this—they too should be spared."
units.literal: Among them were youths; he said: "What do children know—they too should be pardoned."

units.zh: 全活甚眾。
units.en: A great many lives were spared.
units.literal: Very many were thus spared alive.

units.zh: 鄭成功屯廈門，與漳州隔海相望。
units.en: Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the strait.
units.literal: Zheng Chenggong was stationed at Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the sea.

units.zh: 固山額真駐會城，遣兵戍漳州，番代歲四易，民苦供役。
units.en: The garrison commander at the provincial capital sent troops to hold Zhangzhou; reliefs rotated four times a year, and the people groaned under the levies.
units.literal: The garrison commander was stationed at the provincial capital and sent troops to garrison Zhangzhou; rotations changed four times a year, and the people suffered from supplying corvée.

units.zh: 朋舉請駐防無屢更，不許；
units.en: Pengju asked that the garrison not be rotated so frequently; the request was denied.
units.literal: Pengju requested that the garrison not be changed so often; this was not granted.

units.zh: 固請展其期，歲再易，民稍蘇息。
units.en: He pressed hard to lengthen the rotation interval to twice a year, and the people gained some respite.
units.literal: He firmly petitioned to extend the term; rotations came twice a year, and the people found some relief.

units.zh: 擢四川按察使、山東右布政使。
units.en: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and Right Administrative Commissioner of Shandong.
units.literal: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and right administrative commissioner of Shandong.

units.zh: 父憂歸。
units.en: He left office to mourn his father.
units.literal: He returned home upon his father's death.

units.zh: 起授湖南布政使。
units.en: He was recalled to service as administrative commissioner of Hunan.
units.literal: He was recalled and appointed administrative commissioner of Hunan.

units.zh: 上官，見胥吏至數百，曰：「兵初罷，民方重困。
units.en: On taking office he found hundreds of clerks and said: "The armies have only just stood down and the people are in deep distress.
units.literal: Upon assuming office he saw clerks numbering in the hundreds and said: "The troops have only just stood down and the people are in deep distress.

units.zh: 此曹鮮衣美食，縱橫市井間，何所​​取諸？」
units.en: Yet these men dress well, eat well, and swagger through the markets—where does it all come from?"
units.literal: These fellows dress in fine clothes and eat well, swaggering through the markets—where do they get it?"

units.zh: 汰其十九，擇謹願者，取足供文書而已。
units.en: He dismissed nine out of ten, kept only the prudent and dutiful, and retained just enough staff to handle paperwork.
units.literal: He dismissed nineteen out of twenty, chose the prudent and willing, and kept only enough to handle documents.

units.zh: 數為大吏言地方利病，有司賢不肖積與之忤，被劾鐫級，未行，而大吏以貪敗。
units.en: He repeatedly reported local abuses to senior officials; worthy and unworthy magistrates alike resented him; he was impeached and demoted, and before he could depart the senior official himself was ruined for corruption.
units.literal: He repeatedly told high officials of local benefits and harms; officials worthy and unworthy alike accumulated grievances against him; he was impeached and demoted in rank, and before he could leave the senior official was ruined for corruption.

units.zh: 士民惜之。
units.en: Scholars and commoners mourned his loss.
units.literal: Gentry and people regretted it.

units.zh: 尋卒。
units.en: He died not long after.
units.literal: Soon afterward he died.

units.zh: 王天鑑，字近微，直隸萬全人。
units.en: Wang Tianjian, courtesy name Jinwei, came from Wanquan in Zhili.
units.literal: Wang Tianjian, styled Jinwei, was a native of Wanquan in Zhili.

units.zh: 順治三年進士，授山東恩縣知縣。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong.
units.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong.

units.zh: 縣接直隸界，自明季為盜藪，嘗一歲七被寇。
units.en: The county bordered Zhili and had been a bandit haunt since the late Ming; one year it was raided seven times.
units.literal: The county bordered Zhili; since the late Ming it had been a bandit haunt and once suffered seven raids in a single year.

units.zh: 天鑑上官，諭父老曰：「往歲寇至，縣輒不守，由人無固志。
units.en: On taking office Tianjian told the elders: "In past years when bandits came the county always fell because the people had no firm resolve.
units.literal: When Tianjian took office he told the elders: "In past years when bandits came the county always failed to hold, because people had no firm resolve.

units.zh: 自今勿復逃，視知縣所向。」
units.en: From now on do not flee—watch where your magistrate goes."
units.literal: From now on do not flee again; watch where the magistrate goes."

units.zh: 俄而寇大至，天鑑坐城上，從容指揮，寇疑有伏，逡巡去。
units.en: Soon a large band arrived; Tianjian sat on the wall and directed the defense calmly; the bandits suspected a trap and withdrew.
units.literal: Soon bandits came in force; Tianjian sat on the wall and directed affairs calmly; the bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew hesitantly.

units.zh: 於是葺樓櫓，治城隍，嚴候望，時巡徼，守具大備。
units.en: He then repaired towers and battlements, restored the moat, tightened watch posts, patrolled regularly, and made the defenses complete.
units.literal: Thereupon he repaired towers and battlements, restored the city moat, tightened watch and signal posts, patrolled regularly, and defenses were fully prepared.

units.zh: 按行鄉鄙，舉團練，立砦十有九，枹鼓相聞，久之得步卒萬八千、騎士三百。
units.en: He toured the countryside, organized militia, and established nineteen stockades whose drums could be heard from one to the next; in time he fielded eighteen thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry.
units.literal: He toured the countryside, raised militia, established nineteen stockades with drums and gongs within hearing of one another, and in time mustered eighteen thousand foot soldiers and three hundred cavalry.

units.zh: 巡按御史疏聞，令天鑑自治兵。
units.en: The touring censor reported to the throne, and Tianjian was authorized to command troops in his own right.
units.literal: The touring censor memorialized the throne, and Tianjian was ordered to command troops himself.

units.zh: 廉得境內賊渠數輩，夜突至其鄉呼之出，賊錯愕不能遁，皆誅之。
units.en: He traced several bandit chiefs in the district, raided their villages by night, and called them out; caught off guard, they could not escape and were all put to death.
units.literal: He investigated and found several bandit chiefs within the district; by night he suddenly appeared in their villages and called them out; the bandits were startled and could not escape—all were executed.

units.zh: 寇據曹縣，巡撫檄天鑑與諸道兵會剿，率所部為前鋒，冒矢石深入，諸軍踵之，復其城。
units.en: When bandits seized Cao County, the governor ordered Tianjian and allied forces to join the campaign; he led his men as vanguard, pushed through arrow and stone fire, the main force followed, and the city was retaken.
units.literal: Bandits held Cao County; the governor ordered Tianjian and troops from several circuits to join in suppression; he led his own forces as vanguard, braved arrows and stones in deep advance, the armies followed, and the city was recovered.

units.zh: 嘗以輕騎逐賊，日暮被圍，短兵相接，手格殺數賊，潰圍出，不失一騎。
units.en: Once he pursued bandits with a light cavalry detachment; at dusk he was surrounded, fought hand to hand, killed several with his own blade, broke out, and did not lose a single horse.
units.literal: Once with light cavalry he pursued bandits; at dusk he was surrounded, fought hand to hand, personally killed several bandits, broke out of the encirclement, and lost not a single horse.

units.zh: 在恩四年，屢與寇戰，俘馘無算，降者安撫之。
units.en: In four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly, took countless prisoners and heads, and settled those who surrendered.
units.literal: In four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly, took countless prisoners and heads, and pacified those who surrendered.

units.zh: 寇遠遁，招徠屯種，流亡復歸，墾荒千八百頃。
units.en: After the bandits fled he encouraged resettlement and farming; refugees returned and eighteen hundred qing of wasteland were reclaimed.
units.literal: When bandits fled far away he summoned people to settle and farm; refugees returned, and eighteen hundred qing of wasteland were brought under cultivation.

units.zh: 建書院，弦誦不輟。
units.en: He founded an academy where students studied without interruption.
units.literal: He built an academy where study and recitation never ceased.

units.zh: 政聲為山東最，上考，內遷禮部主事。
units.en: His reputation was the finest in Shandong; rated at the top of his evaluation he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites in the capital.
units.literal: His administrative reputation was the finest in Shandong; on superior evaluation he was transferred within the capital to a secretaryship in the Ministry of Rites.

units.zh: 十一年，始行耤田親耕禮，天鑑參酌古今，悉合禮宜。
units.en: In the eleventh year the emperor first performed the sacred-field plowing rite; Tianjian drew on ancient and modern precedents and arranged everything in proper ritual form.
units.literal: In the eleventh year the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field was first performed; Tianjian drew on ancient and modern precedents and all conformed to ritual propriety.

units.zh: 累遷郎中。
units.en: He rose through the ranks to director.
units.literal: He was promoted in stages to director.

units.zh: 主山東鄉試。
units.en: He served as chief examiner for the Shandong provincial examination.
units.literal: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.

units.zh: 十二年，出為陝西河西道參議。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was posted as assistant administrator of Hexi Circuit in Shaanxi.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as assistant administrator of Hexi Circuit in Shaanxi.

units.zh: 與屬吏約，毋獵民枉法。
units.en: He pledged to his staff that they would not prey on the people or pervert the law.
units.literal: He agreed with subordinates not to hunt the people or bend the law.

units.zh: 天鑑固長治兵，按籍討軍實，誡將弁毋以軍糈肥私橐。
units.en: Tianjian was a natural commander; he audited registers to verify troop strength and warned officers against lining their pockets with army grain.
units.literal: Tianjian was by nature skilled at governing troops; he checked registers to verify military strength and admonished officers not to fatten private purses with army grain.

units.zh: 性剛介負氣，數忤上官。
units.en: Proud and unyielding by nature, he often clashed with his superiors.
units.literal: His nature was upright and proud; he often offended superiors.

units.zh: 歲餘，謝病歸。
units.en: After little more than a year he resigned on grounds of illness.
units.literal: After little more than a year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

units.zh: 絕跡公府，門下士或有餽遺，不受，曰：「飭簠簋，惜名節，足以報舉主矣！」
units.en: He kept away from official circles; when disciples offered gifts he refused them, saying: "Keeping my conduct clean and my name intact is repayment enough to those who recommended me!"
units.literal: He vanished from public offices; when disciples sometimes offered gifts he would not accept them, saying: "To keep my vessels in order and cherish my reputation is enough to repay those who recommended me!"

units.zh: 康熙初，大臣薦，不出。
units.en: In the early Kangxi reign ministers recommended him, but he would not return to office.
units.literal: In the early Kangxi reign ministers recommended him, but he would not emerge.

units.zh: 尋卒。
units.en: He died not long after.
units.literal: Soon afterward he died.

units.zh: 趙廷標，浙江錢塘人。
units.en: Zhao Tingbiao came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.
units.literal: Zhao Tingbiao was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

units.zh: 順治三年，以拔貢生授福建永定知縣。
units.en: In the third year of Shunzhi he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian as a selected tribute student.
units.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, as a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian.

units.zh: 廣東大埔逸寇江龍以萬餘人犯縣城，廷標城守。
units.en: The outlaw Jiang Long of Dapu, Guangdong, attacked the county seat with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao held the walls.
units.literal: The fugitive bandit Jiang Long of Dapu in Guangdong invaded the county seat with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao defended the walls.

units.zh: 寇穴地入，瀦池水以待，地砲不得發；
units.en: The bandits tunneled in; he dammed the moat to flood the approaches so land mines could not be detonated.
units.literal: The bandits burrowed underground; he dammed the moat to hold water so land mines could not be fired.

units.zh: 樹雲梯乘城，於城上懸柵墮之。
units.en: They raised siege ladders; he hung barriers along the parapet to drop on them.
units.literal: They raised cloud ladders to scale the wall; he hung barriers above the wall to drop on them.

units.zh: 持三月，食垂盡。
units.en: The siege lasted three months until food was nearly gone.
units.literal: The siege lasted three months and food was nearly exhausted.

units.zh: 值立春，廷標張鼓樂，開城門，迎春東郊。
units.en: At the Beginning of Spring festival Tingbiao staged music, opened the gates, and led the spring rites in the eastern suburbs.
units.literal: When the Beginning of Spring arrived, Tingbiao set out drums and music, opened the city gate, and welcomed spring in the eastern suburbs.

units.zh: 寇疑有伏，引去。
units.en: The bandits suspected a trap and withdrew.
units.literal: The bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew.

units.zh: 密遣兵間道往伏兩山間，出不意夾擊，敗之。
units.en: He secretly sent troops by hidden paths to ambush them between two hills and struck from both sides by surprise, routing them.
units.literal: He secretly sent troops by hidden paths to lie in ambush between two mountains and struck them unexpectedly from both sides, defeating them.

units.zh: 進至龍磜寨，捕斬略盡。
units.en: He pressed on to Longji Stockade and captured or killed nearly all who remained.
units.literal: Advancing to Longji Stockade, he captured and beheaded nearly all of them.

units.zh: 擢湖廣衡州同知，署府事。
units.en: He was promoted to vice prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and acted as prefect.
units.literal: He was promoted to vice prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and acted in prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 蠲賦墾荒，流亡復業。
units.en: He remitted taxes, encouraged reclamation, and brought refugees back to their farms.
units.literal: He remitted taxes and opened wasteland; refugees returned to their occupations.

units.zh: 歲大饑，賑恤有實惠。
units.en: In a year of famine his relief reached those who needed it.
units.literal: In a year of great famine his relief brought real benefit.

units.zh: 經略大學士洪承疇薦廷標，十七年，擢雲南迤東道副使。
units.en: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou recommended Tingbiao; in the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of Yidong Circuit in Yunnan.
units.literal: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, commissioner-general, recommended Tingbiao; in the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice commissioner of Yidong Circuit in Yunnan.

units.zh: 安普諸番為土官所誘，競作不靖。
units.en: The tribes of Anpu, incited by native officials, rose in unrest one after another.
units.literal: The tribes of Anpu, incited by native officials, vied in making trouble.

units.zh: 廷標設方略、行間，解散之，遂復維摩舊地。
units.en: Tingbiao devised strategy and used agents to break them up, and thereby recovered the old Weimo territory.
units.literal: Tingbiao devised strategy and used agents among them to disperse them, and thereby recovered the old territory of Weimo.

units.zh: 移檄諭寧州彌勒、巴盤、八甸，罷捕逐之令，令諸持田器者皆為良民，持兵者乃為賊。
units.en: He issued proclamations to Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, ending the orders to hunt people down, and ruled that anyone holding farm tools was a law-abiding subject while only those bearing arms were bandits.
units.literal: He sent proclamations to Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, abolishing orders to hunt and drive people out, decreeing that all who held farming tools were good people and only those who held weapons were bandits.

units.zh: 巡行安撫，諸路悉平。
units.en: He toured the region to reassure the people, and every route was pacified.
units.literal: He toured to pacify and comfort; all routes were entirely settled.

units.zh: 治迤東十八年。
units.en: He governed Yidong for eighteen years.
units.literal: He governed Yidong for eighteen years.

units.zh: 康熙中，調廣東廣肇南韶道副使。
units.en: During the Kangxi reign he was transferred to vice commissioner of Guangzhaonanxiao Circuit in Guangdong.
units.literal: In the Kangxi reign he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Guangzhaonanxiao Circuit in Guangdong.

units.zh: 安普民、蠻聞其去，塹道塞城留之。
units.en: When the people and tribes of Anpu learned he was leaving, they dug trenches and blocked the gates to keep him from going.
units.literal: When the people and tribes of Anpu heard he was leaving, they dug ditches and blocked the city to detain him.

units.zh: 慰諭再三，乃得行。
units.en: Only after repeated reassurances was he able to leave.
units.literal: After repeated consolation and instruction he was able to depart.

units.zh: 兩粵八排諸山寇聞廷標來，望風解散。
units.en: When the mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in the two Guang provinces heard Tingbiao was coming, they melted away at the news.
units.literal: When the mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in the two Guang provinces heard Tingbiao was coming, they dispersed at the news.

units.zh: 連州亂，至，立就撫。
units.en: Lianzhou was in revolt; when he arrived the rebels submitted at once.
units.literal: Lianzhou was in revolt; when he arrived they immediately submitted to pacification.

units.zh: 逾年以憂去。
units.en: After more than a year he left office to mourn a parent.
units.literal: After more than a year he left on account of mourning.

units.zh: 起湖南驛鹽道副使。
units.en: He was recalled as vice commissioner of the Post and Salt Circuit in Hunan.
units.literal: He was recalled to serve as vice commissioner of the Post and Salt Circuit in Hunan.

units.zh: 捕治劇寇，誅其渠，餘悉縱歸農。
units.en: He captured major bandits, executed their leaders, and sent the rest back to their farms.
units.literal: He captured and punished fierce bandits, executed their leaders, and released the rest to return to farming.

units.zh: 湖南方用兵，芻茭械仗，儲峙供給，不誤晷刻，民不困役。
units.en: Hunan was at war; he supplied fodder, arms, and stores without a moment's delay, and kept corvée burdens from crushing the people.
units.literal: Hunan was then at war; fodder, weapons, and stores were supplied without missing a moment, and the people were not worn down by corvée.

units.zh: 兼攝糧道。
units.en: He also served as acting grain intendant.
units.literal: He also acted as grain intendant.

units.zh: 會湘東民變，巡撫韓世琦令廷標往撫之。
units.en: When eastern Hunan erupted in unrest, Governor Han Shiqi sent Tingbiao to pacify the region.
units.literal: When the people of eastern Hunan rose in disturbance, Governor Han Shiqi ordered Tingbiao to go pacify them.

units.zh: 單騎馳諭，皆悔泣聽命，散遣之。
units.en: He rode out alone to reason with them; they wept, repented, and obeyed, and he sent them home.
units.literal: He rode alone in haste to instruct them; all repented, wept, and obeyed, and he dispersed them.

units.zh: 事稍定，修岳麓書院，置田禀諸生。
units.en: When order returned he restored Yuelu Academy and endowed fields to support its students.
units.literal: When affairs were somewhat settled he restored Yuelu Academy and set aside fields to support students.

units.zh: 嘗行部至衡州，父老羅拜車下，號以「慈母」。
units.en: Once on circuit he reached Hengzhou; elders lined up to bow before his carriage and called him "the loving mother."
units.literal: Once when touring his circuit he reached Hengzhou; elders bowed in rows beneath his carriage and hailed him as "a loving mother."

units.zh: 俄遷陝西糧儲道參議。
units.en: Soon he was transferred to assistant administrator of the Grain Storage Circuit in Shaanxi.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to be assistant administrator of the Grain Storage Circuit in Shaanxi.

units.zh: 已病，值武昌兵變，軍書至，猶強起視事。
units.en: He was already ill; when troops mutinied at Wuchang and dispatches arrived, he still dragged himself to his desk.
units.literal: He was already ill; when the military mutiny at Wuchang broke out and dispatches arrived, he still forced himself up to attend to business.

units.zh: 病篤乞歸，至家卒。
units.en: His illness worsened and he begged to go home; he died as soon as he arrived.
units.literal: His illness grew grave and he begged to return home; he died upon reaching home.

units.zh: 論曰：自置督撫，而兩司權輕，況於各道；
units.en: The commentary says: Once governors-general and governors were established, the authority of the two provincial commissioners grew lighter—and the circuit posts lighter still.
units.literal: The commentary says: Since governors-general and governors were established, the two provincial commissioners grew lighter in authority, and still more the circuit intendant posts.

units.zh: 然以賢者處之，奉職循理，視民之所急，弭亂解嬈，亦足以為治。
units.en: Yet when worthy men hold these posts, perform their duties faithfully, heed what the people urgently need, and quell disorder and ease hardship, that too is government enough.
units.literal: Yet when the worthy hold such posts, fulfilling duty and following principle, looking to what the people urgently need, quelling disorder and relieving distress, that is also enough for good government.

units.zh: 而述、振芬、振姬、天鑑皆有才略，根本尤在廉勤。
units.en: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and strategic ability; above all they were rooted in integrity and diligence.
units.literal: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and strategy; the root lay especially in integrity and diligence.

units.zh: 延著、國棟、廷標當治亂用重之日，濟之以寬仁，雖以是罷貶，甚或中危法，而一不自卹，是皆能舉其職者。
units.en: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao served when governing turmoil demanded stern measures, yet they tempered authority with mercy. Some were dismissed or demoted for it, and some even faced capital charges, but none thought of themselves—these were men who truly did their duty.
units.literal: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao served in days when order and disorder called for stern measures; they supplemented this with leniency and kindness. Though some were dismissed or demoted for it, and some even fell under grave law, none spared themselves—these all were men who could fulfill their duties.

units.zh: 澤及於斯民，亦已多矣。
units.en: The good they did for the people was already very great indeed.
units.literal: The blessings that reached these people were already very great.
